newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SRI LANKA NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
UNIONS CALL OFF BUS STRIKE

Four major transport unions decided to call off their three-day-old strike, which affected public bus services in Sri Lanka, following a new wage agreement with Transport & Highways Minister A. H. M. Fowzie.
Under the agreement, workers will get a retrospective wage increase of 360 rupees per month from January this year.
OVERSEAS STOCK MARKET INVESTMENT FOR LANKANS RECOMMENDED

Sri Lankans should be allowed to invest in overseas stock markets, said Colombo Stock Exchange Chairman Reinzie T. Wijetilleke. Such transactions are currently restricted by the Exchange Controller. Wijetilleke said investors will stand to gain if this restriction is lifted fully or at least to cover the south Asian stock markets..
THE ISLAND
LANKA LOHA TAKEOVER DELAYED BY COMPENSATION ISSUE
The takeover of Lanka Loha Pvt Ltd by Korea's Hanjung Corporation is likely to be delayed since no agreement has been reached on a compensation package for employees who are to be retrenched.
DIVAINA
OPPOSITION LOCAL COUNCILLOR SHOT DEAD

An opposition United National Party (UNP) member of the Beliatta pradeshiya sabha, A.M.K. Gooneratne, was shot dead by an unidentified gunman riding a motor cycle. Police said they were investigating.
RAILWAY TECHNICIANS LAUNCH WORK TO RULE CAMPAIGN

Railaway services in Sri Lanka are likely to be hit due to a proposed work to rule campaign by the railway technicians from midnight on August 14. The technicians' unions said they were resorting to union action after talks with the government for higher wages failed.
DINAMINA
POLICE INVESTIGATES TAMIL TIGER FUNDING

Police is sifting through documents that prove that colossal amounts of government funds were given to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) during the previous UNP regime, in addition to the stocks of arms, ammunition and cement. Several prominent people responsible for these activities are to be arrested soon, a senior police source said.
THINAKKURAL
NEW SINHALA-TAMIL POLITICAL PARTY FORMED
A new political party named "Sri Lanka Tamil - Sinhala United Front" has been formed. The party will work on the platform of ending the country's war, which it says is hitting the economy.
